There's a now-obvious deadlock in KSM's out-of-memory handling:
imagine ksmd or KSM_RUN_UNMERGE handling
trying to allocate a page to break KSM in an mm which becomes the
OOM victim (quite likely in the unmerge case): it's killed and goes
to exit
column2: and hangs there waiting to acquire ksm_thread_mutex.

column1: Clearly we must not require ksm_thread_mutex in __ksm_exit
though that made everything else: perhaps use mmap_sem somehow?
And part of the answer lies in the comments on unmerge_ksm_pages:
__ksm_exit should also leave all the rmap_item removal to ksmd.
But there's a fundamental problem
column2: that KSM relies upon mmap_sem to

column1: guarantee the consistency of the mm it's dealing with
tears down an mm without taking mmap_sem.  And bumping mm_users won't
help at all
column2: that just ensures that the pages the OOM killer assumes

column1: are on their way to being freed will not be freed.
The best answer seems to be
column2: to move the ksm_exit callout from just

column1: before exit_mmap
column2: to the middle of exit_mmap: after the mm's pages

column1: have been freed (if the mmu_gather is flushed)
tables and vma structures have been freed; and down_write
mmap_sem there to serialize with KSM's own reliance on mmap_sem.
But KSM then needs to be careful
check that the mm is not already exiting: there's a danger of using
find_vma on a layout that's being torn apart
tables which have been freed for reuse; and even do_anonymous_page
and __do_fault need to check they're not being called by break_ksm
to reinstate a pte after zap_pte_range has zapped that page table.
Though it might be clearer to add an exiting flag
mmap_sem in __ksm_exit
column2: that wouldn't cover the issue of reinstating

column1: a zapped pte.  All we need is to check whether mm_users is 0 - but
must remember that ksmd may detect that before __ksm_exit is reached.
So
column2: ksm_test_exit(mm) added to comment such checks on mm->mm_users.

column1: __ksm_exit now has to leave clearing up the rmap_items to ksmd
that needs ksm_thread_mutex; but shift the exiting mm just after the
ksm_scan cursor so that it will soon be dealt with.  __ksm_enter raise
mm_count to hold the mm_struct
its processing when it finds all VM_MERGEABLEs unmapped) mmdrop it
similar procedure for KSM_RUN_UNMERGE (which has stopped ksmd).
But also give __ksm_exit a fast path: when there's no complication
(no rmap_items attached to mm and it's not at the ksm_scan cursor)
it can safely do all the exiting work itself.  This is not just an
optimization: when ksmd is not running
otherwise leak mm_structs.
